title: "Leftover Hash Lemma extraction from unpredictable random-oracle sources"
subtitle: "How well does H(sd, x) look uniform, when x comes from an unbounded-but-unpredictable source?"
aliases:
  - "/open-problems/information-theoretic/leftover-hash-lemma-unpredictable-sources/index.html"

## Motivation

Randomness extraction results usually assume the source is independent of the extractor's key. Here the extractor is itself a random oracle $H$, and the source $S$ is allowed to see the *entire* function table of $H$ before choosing its input $x$ (together with side information $z$) -- it's only assumed *unpredictable*, not independent. Two natural games ask how close $H(\mathit{sd}, x)$ then looks to uniform, differing in whether the extraction seed $\mathit{sd}$ is handed to the distinguisher (public seed) or kept hidden (secret seed). Both conjectured bounds take the classical leftover-hash-lemma shape: an entropy-deficiency term plus a seed-collision term that vanishes as $1/\sqrt{K}$ in the number of seeds $K$.

## Provenance and history

Both conjectures were stated together as a single self-contained write-up (statement by Pooya Farshim; see the shared PDF linked from [c/0004](/c/0004/)). The public-seed case was resolved shortly after: an AI-written proof (Claude Opus 5, prompted by Pooya Farshim, 14 August 2026) shows the naive guess -- transposing the secret-seed expression directly to the public-seed game -- is false, and proves a corrected bound instead, with an explicit near-optimal constant. That proof has not yet been independently reviewed by a human, nor formalized. The secret-seed case (Conjecture 1 of the shared write-up) is now tracked as [c/0005](/c/0005/), transcribed from the same PDF; no proof of it is recorded. A bound for it was referenced only informally, via an unincluded and unverified "companion note," in the public-seed resolution's write-up, and that note is still not on the site.

## Parameter lattice

Two independent axes: whether the seed is public or secret, and whether extraction draws from one source or from $k$ sources jointly. Three of the four cells are tracked as their own statement on the site.

| | single source | $k$-source |
|---|---|---|
| **public seed** | [c/0004](/c/0004/) -- proven | [c/0006](/c/0006/) -- *test placeholder* |
| **secret seed** | [c/0005](/c/0005/) -- open | *unstated* |

The single-source public-seed cell is real, cited research. The $k$-source column's public-seed cell ([c/0006](/c/0006/)) is a `category: test` placeholder added to demonstrate the lattice mechanic on a genuine (if unattempted) question, not a claim from any source. The single-source secret-seed cell ([c/0005](/c/0005/)) is Conjecture 1 of the same shared write-up, open. The secret-seed, $k$-source cell is left unstated on purpose: nobody has posed it yet, here or elsewhere that this archive knows of.
